primary_source.title: Option positions, non-momentum trading, and Bitcoin futures returns
primary_source.evidence_boundary: The peer-reviewed paper reports that CFTC asset-manager Bitcoin option positioning selectively predicts second-week-ahead futures returns and that the non-momentum component drives the result. The present raw-change factor is a deliberately simpler transfer test, not a replication of the unavailable residual formula.

source_contract.combined_minus_futures_semantics: Option positions are derived as futures-and-options-combined futures-equivalent positions minus futures-only positions for the identical report date.

performance_case.causal_mechanism: A weekly contraction in asset-manager option net exposure may indicate that the adverse residual positioning pressure documented in the primary study is absent before the second-week decision window.
performance_case.performance_hypothesis: Admitting unchanged equal-capital DRA entries only during option-position contraction may improve fee-adjusted realized and total PnL.
performance_case.drawdown_hypothesis: The filter may avoid adverse second-week paths without increasing maximum drawdown, underwater duration, holding age or terminal inventory.
performance_case.opportunity_cost: If contraction removes profitable DRA participation or the raw change does not inherit the paper's residual predictability, the family must close without residualization or threshold tuning.

stop_conditions: Stop on any source, schema, row identity, exact-date join or pre-outcome availability mismatch.
Stop and close if any frozen Design or Validation predictive or economic gate fails.
Do not residualize, invert, normalize differently, change the seven-day decision clock, tune a threshold or inspect OOS after outcome access.
